questions.question: If you connect two identical bulbs in parallel to a battery, how does their brightness compare to when the same two bulbs are connected in series to the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are brighter than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in series are brighter than the bulbs in parallel.
The bulbs in both circuits have the exact same brightness.
The bulbs in parallel do not light up at all.

questions.question: When comparing two identical bulbs connected in parallel to a battery with the same two bulbs connected in series to the same battery, what is true about the current?
options: The current through the parallel bulbs is smaller than through the series bulbs.
The current through the parallel bulbs is bigger than through the series bulbs.
The current is exactly the same in both circuits.
There is no current flowing in the parallel circuit.

questions.question: How does the voltage across one of two identical bulbs in a parallel circuit compare to the voltage across one of the same bulbs in a series circuit, using the same battery?
options: The voltage is the same across a single bulb in both circuits.
The voltage across the parallel bulb is smaller than across the series bulb.
The voltage across the parallel bulb is bigger than across the series bulb.
The voltage across the parallel bulb is zero.

questions.question: Why does a battery lighting two bulbs in a parallel circuit run out faster than the same battery lighting the same two bulbs in a series circuit?
options: Because the parallel circuit has higher overall resistance, which wastes energy.
Because the parallel circuit transfers energy from the battery more quickly.
Because series circuits store energy inside the bulbs.
Because current only flows through one bulb at a time in parallel.

questions.question: In physics, what is meant by the term 'resistance' in an electrical circuit?
options: The speed at which electrons travel through the battery.
A measure of how difficult it is for an electric current to flow.
The total amount of energy stored in a cell.
The number of loops in a parallel circuit.

questions.question: What is the unit used to measure electrical resistance?
options: Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Watts (W)
Ohms (Ω)

questions.question: How does changing the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
Changing the length has no effect on resistance.
The shorter the wire, the greater its resistance.

questions.question: If you double the length of a piece of metal wire, what happens to its electrical resistance?
options: The resistance stays the same.
The resistance is halved.
The resistance doubles.
The resistance is quadrupled.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the resistance of a uniform wire and its length?
options: Resistance is proportional to its length.
Resistance is inversely proportional to its length.
Resistance is equal to the square of its length.
There is no mathematical relationship between resistance and length.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, what is true about the pathway of each individual loop?
options: Each loop must pass through every component in the circuit.
Each loop can be traced from one end of the cell or battery to the other end.
Each loop is blocked by a switch to prevent current flow.
Each loop must contain its own separate battery.

questions.question: What does the 'power' of an electrical device measure?
options: The total force with which current is pushed.
The total amount of charge stored in the device.
The amount of energy used by or supplied to a device in one second.
The resistance of the device per metre.

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure electrical power?
options: Watts (W)
Joules (J)
Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)

questions.question: How do we calculate the electrical energy used by a device in kilowatt-hours (kWh)?
options: Multiply the power in kilowatts (kW) by the time in hours (h).
Divide the power in watts (W) by the time in hours (h).
Multiply the voltage in volts (V) by the resistance in ohms (Ω).
Add the power in kilowatts (kW) to the time in hours (h).

questions.question: What defines a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit that contains only one bulb and one switch.
A circuit with more than one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit where all components are connected end-to-end in a single line.
A circuit that does not require a power source to function.

questions.question: When drawing a circuit diagram, why is it important to use a ruler and ensure there are no tiny gaps?
options: To ensure the diagram shows that the components are parallel rather than series.
For clarity, and to show there are no breaks in the circuit that would stop current flowing.
To represent the exact physical length of the real wires.
To indicate that the resistance of the wires is zero.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, what is the relationship between the currents in the individual branches and the total current through the battery?
options: The current through each branch is always double the total current.
The current through each branch is equal to the total current.
The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch subtracts from the total current to equal zero.

questions.question: How does the thickness of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The thicker the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The thicker the wire, the greater its resistance.
Thickness has no effect on the resistance of a wire.
Thinner wires always have smaller resistance.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
options: The resistance doubles.
The resistance halves.
The resistance quadruples.
The resistance remains exactly the same.

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure voltage (potential difference)?
options: Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the voltage across each individual branch compare to the voltage across the cell or battery?
options: The voltage across each branch is shared equally and is less than the battery voltage.
The voltage across each branch is the same as the voltage across the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch is double the battery voltage.
The voltage across each branch is zero.
